claims.explanation: Amisulpride is a selective dopamine D2/D3 receptor antagonist, and its antiproliferative selectivity across cancer lines is most plausibly driven by DRD2 (and related dopamine-receptor pathway) expression: lines that express DRD2/D3 and depend on dopamine/GPCR-cAMP signaling are sensitized, while lines lacking the receptor are protected. Supporting this, the transcriptional virtual cell shows amisulpride's signature most similar to the dopamine antagonist eticlopride, and the literature confirms high-affinity D2/D3 antagonism as the drug's core mechanism.

features.basis: amisulpride is a high-affinity DRD2 antagonist; receptor expression is required for target engagement
amisulpride binds DRD3 with high affinity (Ki ~3 nM) and antagonizes D3 receptors
D2 blockade de-represses prolactin secretion; autocrine PRL signaling may sustain viability in responsive lines
constitutive Gs/cAMP signaling downstream of D2-like GPCRs may enhance dependence on dopamine-receptor tone
amisulpride is metabolized by CYP enzymes; high CYP2D6 activity could lower effective intracellular drug exposure
atypical antipsychotic action involves 5-HT2A as well as D2 receptors; co-expression may broaden sensitivity
serotonin receptor modulation contributes to atypical antipsychotic pharmacology and may cooperate with D2 blockade
D2 receptors signal through adenylyl cyclase/cAMP; high ADCY tone may increase dependence on dopaminergic input
D2 antagonist-induced immediate-early gene responses may mark cells with intact dopamine-receptor signaling
dopamine-receptor blockade alters immediate-early gene programs; intact FOS induction may reflect active D2 signaling
CYP3A4 contributes to antipsychotic metabolism and could reduce amisulpride exposure
glucuronidation pathways metabolize antipsychotics and may limit active drug levels
